stage1.impression: A quiet, warm, believable-in-layout night corner: record wall, a lounge chair, a small lamp and one red speaker glowing in the middle. But it reads as a competent CG render, not a photograph. The speaker looks like hot, uniformly lit red plastic rather than thick cast acrylic with polished glowing edges. The concrete is a flat, smooth grey-brown with no formwork grain, tie holes or pools of light. The record spines repeat as a procedural stripe pattern. The foreground chair is a dead black mass, and there is almost no sign of life.

blocking_9: The Ember cabinet must read as thick cast acrylic: bright, polished glowing edges and clean specular reflections, with depth visible through the tint, instead of an evenly lit red box (cabinet lum_p95 - lum_median > 100 at the edges while the faces sit lower)
The board-formed concrete wall must show formwork grain, tie holes and a warm pool of light falling off, not a flat field (falloff across the wall > 25 lum units rather than the current 7)
The horn (the speaker's crown) must be legible as resin with a highlight along its rim, not a dark red blob (median 24 now; needs >= 40)
The foreground chair must show leather sheen and edge light rather than a 15-lum silhouette taking a quarter of the frame
Visible signs of life and the room's own practicals: a glass, a record out of its sleeve, a coat. The fir beams named on the card should be in frame or hinted at
Record spines with real variation (worn, printed, different whites and blacks, some leaning) instead of a repeated stripe texture
Delivered at full resolution with no denoiser smear on the speaker's internal parts or on the screen image

defects.what: Cabinet reads as glossy, evenly lit red plastic. Interior batts and the base block are tinted the same flat red, with no sense of 20+ mm wall thickness and no bright polished edges except a thin line at right
Horn is dark and muddy (median lum 24) with one small plastic-looking streak highlight at lower left (clip 0.24%), so the speaker's crown silhouette is weak
Leather chair is a near-black cutout (median 14.7) with no leather texture, seams or rim light; the dead foreground mass takes about 13% of the frame
Board-formed concrete is flat and smooth: only faint board lines, no tie holes or grain, uniform luminance top to bottom (profile 34 to 41)
Frosted screen panel reads as a soft, blurry print on a wall, with a low-contrast image (lum_range 22). It neither glows like back-lit frosted acrylic nor reads as a thick flush panel
Record spines are a repeating procedural stripe texture: same heights, no lean, no labels, no wear, so the wall looks like a texture
Table lamp dome is an opaque milky white, not smoked acrylic, and the side table has a votive but no glass or other life
Floor and plinth area is murky and featureless; speaker plinth has no contact shadow or floor reflection
No ceiling or fir beams in frame although the card names beams overhead; upper band is empty wall

changes.problem: The Ember reads as an evenly lit red plastic box, not thick cast acrylic: its faces are as bright as its edges and the horn is dark.

evidence.measured: cabinet lum_median 47.3, p95 124, rgb median 92/35/30; horn [235,192,355,262] median 23.9, p95 39; right edge step 28 over 2 px only on one side

change.setting: on each Ember speaker 4 x area lamps
change.from: 4 x area, 10.0 W/m2 at the target, 2900 K, frontal fill
change.to: 2 x narrow strip area lamps as a raking key from upper left and a rim from behind right at 18 W/m2, 2900 K, aimed to graze the cabinet edges and the horn rim; drop the frontal fill to 4 W/m2

changes.expected: Cabinet edges glow brightly while the faces drop slightly darker and deeper, the horn gets a long clean rim highlight, and the acrylic reads thick.

changes.problem: The board-formed concrete is a flat, featureless field with no pool of light, which reads as a CG plaster wall.

evidence.measured: profile y bins 33.8 to 40.7 (falloff about 7); lum_range 32.6

change.setting: concrete finish (tone, sheen) plus sconce point lamp
change.from: smooth low-contrast concrete; sconce 1 x point 20 W
change.to: concrete with stronger board grain bump and roughness variation, tie holes, faint staining, slight sheen (roughness 0.7 varied by +-0.15); sconce 35 W, moved close to the wall so it throws a grazing pool

changes.expected: Board grain and tie holes visible under raking warm light; a pool bright near the sconce falling off to the dark.

changes.problem: The foreground leather chair is a crushed silhouette with no material read.

change.setting: table lamp (EARF Moon) 45 W plus a candle on the chair side
change.from: lamp 45 W, nothing lighting the chair shell
change.to: lamp 60 W, plus one candle (4 W, 1900 K) on the side table nearer the chair; chair leather given a 0.35 roughness sheen

changes.expected: A warm rim along the chair's top edge and arm, leather creases readable, median up to about 22 to 28 while the chair stays the darkest mass.

changes.problem: The frosted screen panel neither glows nor reads as a back-lit thick panel; its image is a blurry low-contrast print.

evidence.measured: lum_median 38.5, lum_range 21.7, same level as the bare wall (38.5)

change.to: 1.6, with the frosted acrylic roughness lowered slightly so the image shows as soft but legible, and the panel's polished edge set to catch the glow

changes.expected: The panel glows evenly and clearly above the wall, its image reads as a fogged form, and its edges show a thin bright line.

changes.problem: The record wall reads as a repeated stripe texture, the strongest single CG tell after the speaker.

evidence.measured: seen at 2x: identical sleeve heights, no lean, regular stripe rhythm in every cubby

change.setting: record wall props and record-wall spots
change.from: uniform procedural sleeves; spots 25 W, 16 deg
change.to: randomised sleeves (height +-3 mm, lean 0 to 8 deg in part-empty cubbies, varied spine colours and whites, a few face-out sleeves); spots 35 W so the top three rows get pools that fall off down the wall

changes.expected: The record wall reads as a real collection with pools of light at the top, falling off downward.

changes.problem: Almost no sign of life, and the side table is bare apart from a votive.

evidence.measured: seen: lamp and one votive only

change.to: a rocks glass with whisky and a record out of its sleeve on the side table, a sleeve leaning against the cabinet base, a coat over the chair arm

changes.expected: The corner reads as used: small highlights in the glass and the vinyl, and the room reads as a bar, not a showroom.

changes.problem: The frame shows no beams and gives a quarter of its width to a black chair, so the speaker is not centred as the hero.

evidence.measured: upper band 0 to 120 is empty wall; chair takes about 13% of the frame at median 15

change.to: position [14.3, 2.7, 1.05] (seated eye level), target [16.3, 4.6, 1.35], 32 mm, verticals kept level by shift rather than tilt so one fir beam enters the top of the frame and the chair is cut to its back edge

changes.expected: Speaker larger and nearer the left third, a beam with checks visible at the top, chair as a framing edge rather than a mass.

changes.problem: The floor and plinth are murky with no contact shadow or reflection anchoring the speaker.

change.to: a slightly polished floor (roughness 0.35) so the speaker throws a soft red reflection and a dark contact shadow; haze 0.035 so the speaker's glow and the lamp spill read in the air

changes.expected: A soft red reflection pooled under the plinth and a darker contact line; a hint of atmosphere around the lamp.

out_of_scope.request: Make the Ember's batts and internal base block read white or less uniformly red
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's parts and tint are fixed; only the light on them may change (c1).

out_of_scope.request: Replace the opaque milky white dome of the table lamp with a visibly smoked acrylic dome
out_of_scope.why: EARF Moon is an EARF product and fixed. If the render shows it wrongly (milky instead of smoked), that is a model or material fidelity issue for the owner to check, not a critic change.
